{"design":"Resolved by reading binary-live-stream.md §1 on 2026-11-22, which answers the question this bead's description called 'the first question'.

THE LIVE STREAM IS NOT A TRANSPORT, so RFC 8887 does not compete with it. §1 says so in as many words: 'Its purpose is to find gaps in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00. Writing every operation again without JMAP's conventions (Session, /get and /changes, state strings, base64url in JSON, SetErrors) shows what the draft leaves to JMAP and what it does not say at all. It is not a transport upgrade.' Its main output is the findings log. RFC 8887 carries JMAP method calls WITH JMAP's conventions, which is precisely what the live stream exists to do without, so adopting RFC 8887 for the agent-to-provider hop would destroy the instrument's purpose rather than modernise it. An earlier note of mine offered retiring the live stream as a plausible reading; it is not, and that was written before reading this rationale.

SETTLED, therefore, without needing Mark's decision:
- RFC 8887 WebSocket goes at the AGENT's endpoint, serving JMAP Chat methods to a client that wants one socket instead of HTTP plus EventSource. Nowhere else.
- The live stream stays exactly as it is, agent to provider, behind its switch, as a second binding of the same operations for finding draft gaps.
- ChatTypingEvent and ChatPresenceEvent are REFUSED, permanently and not merely deferred: mimi-content-10 defines neither typing nor presence (checked, the only hits are the word in passing and two bibliography entries), and inventing them would break AGENTS.md's rule against adding what the spec does not define. The capability advertisement must therefore not claim them, and the draft may want a note that a deployment whose content layer has no presence advertises the transport alone.

PRIORITY: late. No known JMAP Chat client asks for a WebSocket, EventSource already works for clients, and the draft's value here is the transport clause rather than the two event types. Pick it up when a client wants it, or when Mark says otherwise."}

{"notes":"RECONCILED 2026-11-23 with decision mimid-1wgh.122, which asked this
bead's question again without finding it. THIS BEAD IS THE RECORD; .122
is closed as a rediscovery, and what it adds is noted here.

WHAT .122 GOT TO INDEPENDENTLY, and this bead already said: RFC 8887 at
the AGENT's endpoint, serving the user's client, and nowhere else. Same
answer, reached from the other end -- .122 came at it from a call that
cannot connect, this bead from reading the draft.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED, and it is this bead's own PRIORITY clause: "No
known JMAP Chat client asks for a WebSocket, EventSource already works
for clients ... Pick it up when a client wants it, or when Mark says
otherwise." That premise is now false. A calling client wants it, and it
is not a preference: draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 specifies VTCCallSignal as
an ephemeral WebSocket event, the agent's EventSource carries RFC 8620
§7.3 StateChange objects ("these types changed, go look"), and a signal
is not stored so there is nothing to look at (decision mimid-1wgh.117:
signalling is not content). Without the socket a client sends an offer
and waits forever. So this is no longer late; it is the blocking piece
of bead mimid-1wgh.114.8.

WHAT THIS BEAD DID NOT CONTEMPLATE, and is the one open question: it
scopes RFC 8887 to the JMAP CHAT methods. VTCCallSignal belongs to a
different capability -- urn:ietf:params:jmap:vtc:websocket, from
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-wss-00 -- so the socket is one transport carrying
two capabilities' traffic. That is how RFC 8887 is meant to work (it
carries JMAP method calls and the Session advertises what the account
has), but the consequences for this bead:
- the Session advertises BOTH urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:websocket and
  urn:ietf:params:jmap:vtc:websocket, each only when its own capability
  is on the account, and vtc:websocket only when the VTC surface is
  switched on (decision mimid-1wgh.119);
- the subscribe control messages of jmap-chat-wss and the stream-enable
  of jmap-vtc-wss are separate mechanisms on one socket, and neither
  draft says what a server does when a client uses one and not the
  other. Worth a sentence in whichever draft is edited next.

WHAT STAYS REFUSED, unchanged: ChatTypingEvent and ChatPresenceEvent.
mimi-content-10 defines neither, and the capability advertisement must
not claim them."}
